And that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

The “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor shows off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

End-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm

Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ

James wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

Oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

What a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

Nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

The game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

Chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

Aina launches a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”

When asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a big believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s new head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

#2143. Several players needing bounce-back performances: The five key battles in Genoa vs. Milan

AC Milan will make the trip to the Stadio Luigi Ferraris to face a Genoa side in good recent form in a Sunday matinee.

For Milan, it is a familiar feeling of having to bounce back at the weekend after a midweek defeat. The Bournemouth loss was followed up by a win over Udinese, then the collapse against Bologna preceded the derby win.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The most recent setback against Ferencvaros on Thursday has left another bitter feeling, so now Ruben Amorim must galvanise his team again. It will not be an easy one by any stretch though, given Genoa have won four of their last five under Daniele De Rossi, and three in a row.

Speaking of needing a bounce-back, Adrien Rabiot was disappointing in the loss against the Hungarian side. Nonetheless, the Frenchman has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. Sergej Milinkovic-Savic was the last to get as many in the first nine Serie A games back in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Rabiot has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven). His opponent today will be Morten Frendrup, someone that Milan have been repeatedly linked with over the years. The Dane remains Genoa’s metronome in midfield, and the shield in front of the back three.

Summer signing Milutin Osmajić has been Genoa’s main threat in quite a low-scoring side, with four goals to his name in Serie A. He is keeping Lorenzo Colombo out of the side, though the Italian has provided a couple of assists for the Montenegrin when they have been fielded together in a front two.

After a disastrous performance against Ferencvaros, Koni De Winter will be hoping for a much better outing this afternoon. The Belgian has been in the headlines for rejecting a Belgium call-up meaning he will stay over the break, and he will aim to channel that same display against Marcus Thuram in the derby.

In addition to Rabiot, the other player to establish himself as a major threat for Milan is Diego Moreira. The Belgian has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for the Rossoneri, and that came after a bit of a slow start too. He was decisive in the derby, with two assists and a beautiful free-kick goal.

He is expected to have quite a free-ranging role on the right, but what will be very important is getting players around Goncalo Ramos to try and unlock the Portuguese. So, Moreira will likely come up against the left-sided centre-back Johan Vasquez, someone who has become a mainstay in the Genoa side having entered his fifth season there. He does have three bookings in his first nine games, so that could be something to target.

Speaking of Goncalo Ramos, the concerns about his scoring form (or lack thereof) are beginning to grow into full-blown panic. He still has only two Serie A goals to his name so far, one of which was a penalty, and his overall involvement in the Rossoneri’s attacking play seems to be fluctuating between very little and non-existent.

Amorim and the team must get him firing, or it will continue to look like €70m+ spent very badly. Today will not be an easy duel for the former PSG man either as he faces Leo Ostigard, someone who will be well up for the physical battle. As we have seen, Ramos can get frustrated when he faces players who man-mark him, so he will have to be smart and sharp with his movement, ideally getting some more service too.

With an honourable mention going to Christian Pulisic vs. Alessandro Marcandalli, we had to end by mentioning Stephan El Shaarawy. He scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for Milan, becoming a fan favourite during his time. The winger has also become the main creative force for the Grifone, having provided an assist in each of his last two league appearances.

Given his propensity to cut inside in order to create danger, both Mario Gila but especially Yunus Musah will have to watch the 34-year-old very closely indeed. Milan have been exposed in transition several times this season, and there is no doubt El Shaarawy would love to make a statement against his old club.

#2142. Sheffield Wednesday decision Dave Challinor made in midweek has split opinion

Dave Challinor fielded an incredibly young, inexperienced side with numerous debuts handed out as their EFL Trophy group phase ended in heavy defeat against League Two side Accrington Stanley, and the decision to do so has split fan opinion.

Wednesday headed into Wednesday's clash already through in the Northern Group A of the Jersey Mike's Trophy, owing to wins over Sunderland's Under-21s and Salford City over the last international break.

Therefore, new Owls boss Challinor took Wednesday's clash with Accrington as an opportunity to rest some senior players, as various members of the squad battle injury, and hand some academy members an evening they'll never forget, making their debuts at Hillsborough.

The oldest outfield player was 21-year-old Gabriel Otegbayo, and an Accy side that had a mix of teenagers and 39-year-old Shaun Whalley leading the line took advantage to win 4-0 and steal the top spot in the group.

The defeat means that Dave Challinor opens his managerial account at Hillsborough with two defeats in different competitions to League Two opposition, but unlike at Oldham Athletic last Sunday in the FA Cup, this loss against Accrington could have a small asterisk beside it.

Reflecting on the game after the final whistle, Challinor put the onus on a proud night for the academy, with Louis Poland making his senior debut from the off, and Charlie Liddell, Kleven De Oliveira, James Kay, Kailen Hatfield and Fortune Onoh adding to that off the bench.

Barnsley 0-1 Sheffield Wednesday (after extra time), Wembley, 29 May 2023. Type the surnames of Darren Moore's starting XI. Every player you get drops onto the pitch.

You have 90 seconds. Surnames are enough.

Josh Windass headed in Lee Gregory's cross in the 123rd minute to send the Owls up.

"If there's anything to take from it, it's that [a debut at Hillsborough]," he said.

"So whether it's families here, parents, all those sorts of things, I'm sure it will be a night they'll all remember, perhaps not the result they'd want to remember, but the opportunity to play for this club and in this stadium will live with them for the rest of their lives."

It may not have been the ideal result, but the young Wednesday group battled well at 0-0 for 38 minutes, and two late goals from substitutes Charlie Warren and Charlie Caton added some extra gloss to the scoreline for the League Two side.

The majority of the Wednesday fanbase appreciate the decision made by their new manager to hand out debuts and give some senior players a much-needed rest ahead of a return to league action against Plymouth Argyle on Saturday.

"Nothing to lose from tonight. Both clubs are still through to the first round of the sandwich trophy. An ideal time to put youngsters out and see how they fare. As it was a nothing game. Nothing to prove tonight, at all," one fan stated on X.

Another fan commented, "We had already qualified why would he risk any of our first team. Give the kids a run out, move on 🤷🏽‍♂️."

However, there are still some of the more demanding sections of the fanbase who expect Sheffield Wednesday to be competitive in every game they play, and for those who attended the game, they didn't feel as if they got their money's worth.

"Ahhh well, so long as the parents had a good time that's alright," one fan commented in a sarcastic tone, while another added, "Great for the youngsters and their families, but what about the Mugs like me who drove an hour in each direction and paid good money to watch a competitive football match!"

"I know he’s brand new to the post and the game didn’t matter. Losing 4-0 at home to Accrington Stanley is bad in whatever competition #swfc," was also amongst the discourse after the game.

What do you make of Dave Challinor's squad selection on Wednesday night? Let us know in the comments.

However valid you feel both sides of the coin are, it can be agreed that the exposure of some of Wednesday's next generation is, ultimately, a good thing for the club, and Challinor shouldn't, and won't be, judged by this defeat in a competition they'd already qualified out of the group in.

Ultimately, it was a wise decision from Challinor not to risk an already injury-plagued senior squad in a rather meaningless matchup with Accrington Stanley on Wednesday night, especially with the Owls in league action this weekend.

Despite having more than three players out on international duty, not all of them qualify under the EFL quota to warrant a postponement, so Sheffield Wednesday will take on Plymouth in a massive matchup at Hillsborough on Saturday.

FLW gets AI to rank the friendliest clubs in the second tier this season

While Wednesday fans may not have minded an FA Cup run or a more competitve matchup in Challinor's first home game in charge, this is ultimately going to be the game where reactionary early verdicts are given over whether this Owls side will be skyrocketing up the division under their new boss.

Argyle sit three points ahead of Wednesday in the play-offs, so a statement win over Tom Cleverley's side could see the Owls jump back into the top six in Challinor's first game in charge.

It'll be a more energised senior side, given their lack of involvement in midweek, infront of a packed Hillsborough expecting an end to their six-game winless run.

#2141. Max Lowe breaks silence as Sheffield Wednesday situation changes

Dave Challinor has taken over from Henrik Pedersen as the manager of Sheffield Wednesday, and he may find it a bigger challenge than he first thought.

The Owls were defeated by Oldham Athletic of League Two in Round One of the FA Cup last weekend despite lining up with a strong team, before a more youthful side were hammered 4-0 by Accrington Stanley in the EFL Trophy.

Challinor is still yet to take in a league game, which comes this weekend against Plymouth Argyle on home soil, and he'll soon welcome back his former Stockport County favourite Louie Barry into his plans, having been sidelined since early September with an ankle injury.

But with Barry heading back to fitness, Challinor is now having to deal with one more injury to a key player at the opposite end of the pitch.

One of Sheffield Wednesday's key players for a number of years now has been Max Lowe - the left-sided defender has been a top performer and has stuck with the club through their tough period when he could've easily left for another side.

EFL expert Don Goodman has revealed the three clubs across all three tiers to have surprised him the most so far in 2026/27 to Football League World

If there's one drawback to Lowe though, it's his injury record. The defender missed the final eight games of his debut 2024-25 season with a knee injury, and in 2025-26 he'd miss a full three months with a calf problem.

More setbacks followed in late August this year when Lowe suffered with a hamstring injury, and after returning to action a month ago, it's now been revealed that the 29-year-old has yet again suffered a reoccurrence of the problem he picked up two-and-a-half months ago.

Lowe entered the Oldham defeat from the bench after 71 minutes at the weekend, and whilst finishing the entirety of extra time at Boundary Park, the after-effects of his injury means that he's going to be missing for at least four weeks, and potentially up to six.

The Owls and Challinor himself could do with Lowe back for the busy Christmas period, where they'll play three times between Boxing Day and New Year's Day, but given it's his second spell on the sidelines already this season, it's likely that no risks will be taken with the ex-Sheffield United left-back.

And Lowe himself has taken to his Instagram account to send a message to Owls fans regarding his new injury, and it's one that's come from the heart.

Some Sheffield Wednesday fans have been left frustrated at Lowe's newest injury though, with one claiming that he should've been replaced in the summer knowing what his fitness record was like.

And another Owls supporter believes that the medical department itself may need a complete overhaul, given the amount of niggling injuries that keep flaring up across the squad.

If Wednesday were playing in a back four under Challinor, then Reece James would be the obvious replacement like-for-like with Lowe, and that would be the case too in what looks to be the manager's preferred left of a back three.

However, James is also on the sidelines right now, having suffered a groin injury, and he's also expected back around the same time as Lowe.

It'll now likely be Sil Swinkels who comes in for Lowe on the left-hand side of a back three, having served his one-match suspension for a red card against Blackpool, although he too has already had a period on the treatment table.

Challinor may of course look to play a back four in some matches, given his last few months at Stockport saw him pivot to more of a 4-3-3 and sometimes a 4-4-2 given the attacking options he had to choose from, but for now, it may make more sense to utilise the 3-4-2-1, with Jordi Liongola and Yan Valery operating as wing-backs.

#2140. Four away wins in a row and 10 unbeaten: All the key stats ahead of Genoa vs. Milan

Genoa and AC Milan will face off for the 157th time in history on Sunday afternoon at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris in Liguria.

Milan are looking to build on their 71 wins in the fixture, while Genoa are quite far behind with 37 wins, and there have been 48 draws. That being said, in the last five games there have been three ties (3-3, 0-0 and 1-1).

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The good news for the Rossoneri is that they won the other two games in that run, and the five games before that were all wins as well, with no defeat recorded against the Grifone since 2020.

The most recent win was a 2-1 win at the Marassi in favour of Milan, courtesy of goals from Christopher Nkunku and Zachary Athekame. In the game at San Siro, Rafael Leao rescued a point in the dying minutes after Colombo had given Genoa the lead in the first half.

You can read our pre-match preview ahead of an important game before the international break, plus some insight on the resurgent opponents, while below are the best stats ahead of the game.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

➤ Milan have won each of their last four Serie A away games against Genoa. Only against three teams do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

➤ Genoa are on a three-game winning streak in Serie A. The last time the Rossoblu recorded a streak of four consecutive wins in a single season in the top flight was between March and April 2009.

➤ Genoa have won three of their first six home games this season (D1 L2). The Rossoblu haven’t won four of their first seven Serie A home games since the 2015-16 season, when Gian Piero Gasperini was in charge.

➤ Ruben Amorim’s Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 Serie A games this season. The last Rossoneri manager to do better after his first 11 league games was Cesare Maldini in 1972, with 25 goals.

➤ Milan have won two and drawn three of their first five away games this season. The Rossoneri have avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

➤ Genoa have scored four goals in the first 15 minutes of Serie A action this season, a figure they share with Frosinone, Atalanta, Lazio, and Roma and second only to Milan (five). However, the Rossoblu are the only team yet to score in the final 15 minutes of a match.

➤ Stephan El Shaarawy, who scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for AC Milan, has provided an assist in each of his last two Serie A appearances. Should he also contribute to a goal in his next match, he would become, at 34 years and 12 days, the second-oldest player to achieve this feat in three consecutive games for Genoa since 2004-05, after Domenico Criscito in 2021 (34 years and 269 days).

➤ Adrien Rabiot has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. The last midfielder to do better in the first nine games of a Serie A season was Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Furthermore, the Frenchman has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven).

➤ Diego Moreira has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for AC Milan. Since 2004/05, no player has had more in his first six league games for the Rossoneri, equaling Mario Balotelli’s record (seven in 2013).

#2139. Jamie Carragher & Gary Neville discuss one thing they 'don't like' in the EFL

EFL supporters will tend to disagree on most topics, but amid the incessant discourse and fierce daily debates, there is one thing that the majority of fans sing from the same hymn sheet with.

Club and player performance, divisional standards, club size, fanbase volume and stature and hit-or-miss signings are all subjects which invariably promise to polarise and split opinion, yet that's not the case for every single EFL-related matter.

As such, one notable topic may often spark discussions among supporters of League One and League Two clubs but they rarely disagree on it, and their school of thought also has backing from two of the nation's most prominent pundits in Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville.

That subject is, of course, the EFL trophy, which currently goes under the name of the 'Jersey Mike's Trophy' and is contested by clubs in League One and League Two alongside 16 Category One Premier League under-21 sides.

The formatting of the competition includes one academy team for each group, of which there are a total of 16 on a regionalised basis with eight northern and eight southern, and the top two progress to the knockout stages. All fixtures are regionalised until the semi-final stages, with the final two sides ultimately battling it out for silverware at Wembley.

For a number of reasons, however, the EFL trophy and the requirement of each EFL club outside the Championship to compete in the tournament has long represented a point of often-frustrated discussion, and exactly how Carragher and Neville feel about it has become clearer.

Speaking on the latest episode of The Overlap's Stick to Football podcast, the high-profile punditry pair began the show by discussing the participation of Carragher's son James in the competition for Wigan Athletic's 2-1 Group B victory at Crewe Alexandra on Tuesday evening.

Carragher revealed that he switched the match off at half-time, before Neville disclosed that he doesn't like the competition through his boardroom role with League Two leaders Salford City - who lifted the trophy over Portsmouth behind-closed-doors at Wembley back in 2021.

The ex-Liverpool defender explained: "He (James) played last night. It was on at 7 o'clock, you can get it on Sky and he told me he was playing 45 minutes.

"I just switched it off at half time, so I missed the second half. They won 2-1, I think they had already qualified anyway.

Neville then added: "I don't like that trophy. It's a weird one."

Carragher responded that "it's probably a bit like the Carabao Cup for Premier League teams, but when you get to see something at Wembley," to which Neville recounted: "We (Salford) won it in COVID in League Two, we beat Portsmouth at Wembley.

"We were playing in the final against Portsmouth, it was going to be in March and, when lockdown came in February, they'd sold 32,000 tickets for the final and we were going to make quite a lot of money out of it because we'd sold five or six (thousand).

"It was looking at about 40,000, which is a decent crowd at Wembley and the money splits halfway. We ended up playing it the year after infront of no people, the directors and owners were in there but there was literally nobody in the ground and we had to sit two seats apart from each other.

Football League World assesses and ranks the FIFTEEN best away fanbases in the EFL right now

"We absolutely battered them, it was mad."

The EFL Trophy presents a variety of drawbacks for contestants as EFL outfits face much more jeopardy and risk than the competing under-21 sides, which is a key reason as to why many have slammed the tournament over the years.

Understandably, it is widely felt that the now-11-year-old decision to include Category One academy contingents undermines and devalues the competition's integrity and has created a tournament which is essentially designed to accommodate Premier League clubs, despite the fact that no under-21 side has ever lifted the trophy at Wembley.

Indeed, many age-group contestants will actually take prestigious youth tournaments such as the UEFA Youth League and Premier League International Cup more seriously, which only reduces the competitiveness of the EFL Trophy.

Therefore, the matchday experience for EFL Trophy encounters pales in comparison to any league fixture, as matches are often marked by extremely low attendances and non-existent atmospheres in near-empty stadiums in an accurate display of precisely how most EFL clubs and fanbases alike value the competition.

Another prominent issue is how it provides additional fixture congestion in already-hectic schedules, which proves particularly challenging for sides with weaker or lighter squads.

Naturally, it's frequently to the frustration of promotion-chasing or relegation-battling League One and League Two sides when they have to hop out of league action to compete for the trophy when much greater outcomes and jeopardy are on the line.

Be honest, how do you feel about the EFL Trophy? Do you think that all League One and League Two clubs should have to compete? What would you change about it? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

EFL rules mandate the fielding of a minimum number of experienced players, and some clubs can feel the benefits of promoting young talent into senior football through the competition, but the injury risks and fixture congestion often outweigh the advantages and you would be hard-pressed to find too many third and fourth-tier outfits who genuinely value their own participation.

The disadvantages of the EFL Trophy certainly outstrip the benefits for the overwhelming majority of EFL participants, though it's not all universally negative.

Quite obviously, the major upside is the prospect of lifting a trophy at Wembley. We're hardly talking about prestigious silverware here, of course, but either way, that opportunity is one that is nigh-on impossible to experience in any other fashion for almost any non-Championship EFL side unless they win the play-offs, though that's not a classic-style tournament.

Just how much of a benefit that really is remains open to debate, as with only one team capable of winning it per season by definition, everybody else misses out and fails to obtain such an exclusive advantage.

Few would say that trying to get to Wembley in a second-rate competition is of superior importance than trying to battle for promotion or against relegation, too, yet it's a rare upside that can provide supporters with something of a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity.

As aforementioned, meanwhile, the ability to integrate young academy-honed prospects who may not yet be reared and readied for consistent league action into a senior footballing competition, albeit one with debatable pedigree and competitiveness, is still not to be sniffed at.

It can have positive long-term effects, even if the short-term risks mean most clubs would perhaps wish to simply not participate in the first place.

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Tel decides to shoot from range after Charlton clear a corner but the Frenchman’s effort is straight at Brooks

Play has resumed in north London, with Tottenham 2-0 up over Charlton.

They are back under way at St James’ Park and there has been a goal within a few minutes of the second half starting. Newcastle were 1-0 down against West Brom but they now lead 2-1 thanks to Barnes’ goal.

Possession: Tottenham 76%-24% CharltonShots: 9-2Shots on target: 4-1Corners: 7-2Touches in opposition box: 25-2

The first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Whilst they are still in added time in north London, it is half-time at St James’ Park and Newcastle are level 1-1 with West Brom.

Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

Due to a few Charlton injuries, there will be six added minutes.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Tottenham have their second just before the break. Charlton fail to clear their lines inside their own box before Solanke volleys in on the swivel from the penalty spot. Charlton will feel that was definitely an avoidable goal.

Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Moore then strikes it powerfully with his left foot and the ball flies into the roof of the net. Could Brooks have done better in the Charlton goal? Moore will not care.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

Tottenham are currently too slow in possession and are not moving the ball quickly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

West Brom had taken the lead at St James’ Park but Newcastle are back on level terms through summer signing Toure.

A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the hosts as Bergvall cynically takes down Apter as the Charlton man drove towards the Tottenham penalty area. You feel like Charlton need to take advantage of opportunities like this if they want to win this tie. The ball is clipped in and it comes off Van Hecke’s head for a corner. Tottenham clear their lines initially but Charlton keep it alive. Docherty strikes it first time from the edge of the Tottenham box and forces Kinsky into a good save diving to his left.

That probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

Roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

There has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

A sensational free-kick from Isaac Price to give West Brom the lead at St. James' Park! 🤯Watch the Carabao Cup here! - https://t.co/4BMyhp9stB pic.twitter.com/Pnt78LWFN6

Things have just gone from bad to worse for Charlton. Whilst one of their centre-backs is being stretchered off in Sichenje, their other centre-half Koumetio, who used to be on the books at Liverpool, is also down. Koumetio, like Sichenje, is going to come off. McNamara and Jones, who like Koumetio used to be at Liverpool, are coming on. Charlton have had to change both centre-backs inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Sichenje did try to continue but he has gone back down again and his night appears to be over. The question will be has he done more damage to his knee trying to play on? The stretcher is being brought on and it will be a sorry end to his night.

Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and we are just moments away from kick-off north London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Davies, Udogie; Fernandes, Bentancur, Bergvall; Moore, Solanke, Tel. Substitutes: Dubravka, Robertson, Danso, Gallagher, Richarlison, Savio, Porro, Van de Ven, Williams-Barnett.

Charlton: Brooks, Shichenje, Koumetio, Mesik, Asilmwe, Knibbs, Ouma, Apter, Docherty, Alli, Mbick.Substitutes: Okonkwo, Jones, Coventry, Leaburn, Carey, McNamara, Rankin-Costello, Nwamba, Tagoe.

“Tottenham are a top club. Top manager and players so it is a wonderful opportunity to test ourselves. We need to be organised and in the moments we have we want to use our structure to carry a threat. We want to see our structure coming through because we want to evolve. We are a way off these yet, but that is eventually the goal.”

"They got what they deserved"Jamie Redknapp on Spurs' opening day loss against Brentford 😤 pic.twitter.com/mLEb1cCF1x

"I would like to see a reaction"Roberto De Zerbi speaks ahead of Spurs vs Charlton 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/dVIqQBG3wV

After nine years at Anfield, Andy Robertson has swapped Liverpool for Tottenham this summer. He started for Tottenham against Brentford and is on the bench tonight ahead of what could be his first home game for the club.

Omar Marmoush will undergo a medical at Tottenham Hotspur on Wednesday on loan with an obligation to pay Manchester City £60m for the Egypt forward next summer.

Marmoush will become the second signing from City this week after Savinho – who has asked to be referred to as Sávio – completed his move.

City signed Marmoush two seasons ago from Eintracht Frankfurt for £59m and the German club do not have a sell-on clause, meaning they will not receive a fee from the deal.

Our Spurs side to face Charlton! 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/yQuEVgkHbm

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#2137. GdS: Cisse and Jashari among six to draw Amorim’s wrath after Ferencvaros loss

Ruben Amorim was furious after AC Milan’s defeat to Ferencvaros on Thursday night, and some players drew his wrath more than others.

La Gazzetta dello Sport recall that Amorim deemed the performance to be ‘simply unacceptable’, a phrase he used in multiple post-match interviews. The concept was then reiterated in even more direct tones in the dressing room to the team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Beyond the words, Amorim wanted to understand, looking into the eyes of his players after the game, deeming them to be the reason for such a disappointing performance. Alphadjo Cisse, Ardon Jashari, Yunus Musah and the captain Adrien Rabiot are four specifically named.

The Portuguese pressed his players on why – after such an exhilarating victory as the derby – a display like that followed. As he explained post-match, the first topic the coach touched on was the approach.

From the opening minutes, the Rossoneri seemed at the mercy of the Hungarian’s pressing, incapable of finding solutions, ending the first half without a single shot on target. The team’s attitude wasn’t appreciated, nor that of some individuals.

Cisse, one of the key players in the start of the season and fresh from his first call-up to the national team, stood out only for his yellow card and was substituted at half-time, despite having played just a handful of minutes in the derby.

The Italian is barely 20 years old, and Amorim has already preemptively ‘pulled his ears’ to prevent him from getting too excited about his meteoric start. On Thursday, his substitution after 45 minutes said even more than the Portuguese coach’s post-match speech.

In the same boat as Cisse are Davide Bartesaghi, Filippo Terracciano, Jashari and Musah. Amorim is not necessarily pointing the finger exclusively at those who play less and started from the start against the Hungarians.

“The rotation has nothing to do with it,” the former Manchester United manager stated clearly in the press conference after the defeat. Also because, if the first half was a horror, the defeat was sealed in the second half when Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic came on.

Now all eyes immediately turn to the away match in Genoa, the last match before the international break. The topic wasn’t touched upon during Amorim’s meeting with the team at San Siro, but it’s clear that the whole thing was a prelude to an immediate reaction at the Ferraris.

#2136. 'I've seen him crying' - Sam Clucas reveals Nathan Jones truth at Stoke City

Charlton Athletic boss Nathan Jones has never been one to hide his true emotions, with the Welsh boss wearing his heart on his sleeve, as former Stoke City midfielder Sam Clucas has revealed exactly what he is like behind the scenes.

Nathan Jones has cultivated an excellent coaching career for himself, working his way up the ranks at Yeovil Town, Charlton, and Brighton & Hove Albion before taking the top job at Luton Town, guiding the Hatters from League Two to League One.

He'd leave Kenilworth Road for Stoke City in January 2019, with Luton sat 2nd in the third-tier table at the time and the Potters struggling in the Championship following relegation from the Premier League.

His time at the bet365 Stadium went far from planned, but not for lack of trying, as revealed by former midfielder Sam Clucas.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top 25 most demanding fanbases in British football right now

Clucas, 36, is now without a club as he enters the twilight of his playing career, but having worked his way up from the National League with Hereford United to Hull City in the Premier League, he joined Swansea City in the summer of 2017 for £16.5 million.

His time in South Wales didn't go as he had hoped, and 12 months later, he joined Stoke in the Championship for £6 million, initially under former Derby County boss Gary Rowett. Six months later, Jones was appointed as the Potters' new head coach, and Clucas has revealed exactly what he was like behind the scenes.

Speaking to The Football Lowdown podcast, Clucas said: "I loved him, to be honest with you.

"I think you'll see from a lot of his interviews that he's definitely a heart-on-his-sleeve type of guy, and believe me, that's not just for show.

"I've seen him crying in dressing rooms after games and stuff; a really emotional guy, but he puts his heart and soul into everything every day in training, his meetings, everything.

"I wanted it to work out so badly for him, to be honest with you, at Stoke, because you could see how much work he was putting in, and I believe he actually slept over at the training ground a few times."

Having succeeded Rowett at the helm in the Potteries, Jones would guide Stoke to 16th in the Championship that year, and over the summer the likes of Nick Powell, Jordan Cousins, Adam Davies, and Liam Lindsay joined under his watch.

However, the Welshman failed to get a tune out of his side, winning two of his first 14 league games in charge the following campaign and was swiftly dismissed.

With a win percentage of just 15.79 per cent, only Paul Lambert and Chris Kamara have a worse win percentage than Jones for Stoke, and of managers to have undertaken 20 games or more for the Potters, he is statistically the worst of all time.

Whenever he and Stoke meet, there is no love between the Welshman and the Potters' supporters, as despite his best efforts, he ultimately flopped in North Staffordshire.

Since leaving Stoke, Jones has returned to Luton, and followed that up with a brief spell with Southampton and now Charlton, with whom he has helped to establish in the Championship after winning promotion with the Addicks back in 2025.

Jones has tended to thrive as an underdog during his coaching career, and taking the Stoke job with the Potters just having been relegated from the Premier League, it was a disastrous fit for all parties.

The Welshman is certainly not the most popular of head coaches, though his heart-on-the-sleeve personality certainly makes for some box office moments, as he looks to steer Charlton up the second tier table this season.

#2135. Rangers transfer hurdle emerges for both West Ham & Wolves with Ryan Naderi

West Ham United and Wolverhampton Wanderers are looking to bolster their forward options this January, as the Championship promotion hopefuls look north of the border for a Czech goal machine.

West Ham and Wolves are preparing for the January window, and have both seemingly earmarked their centre-forward areas as one that requires some improvement, with Rangers striker Ryan Naderi entering the Championship duo's radar.

Naderi has been in excellent form for the Glasgow-based outfit this season, and could be set for a big money move to England this winter, though West Ham and Wolves seemingly face an uphill battle to secure his services with Rangers not willing to sell.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top 25 most demanding fanbases in British football right now

According to TEAMtalk, both West Ham and Wolves have registered an interest in Czech striker Naderi, with the 23-year-old enjoying an excellent campaign under Derek McInnes at Rangers.

Having spent time coming through the ranks at Dynamo Dresden and Borussia Mönchengladbach in Germany, Naderi propelled himself into the spotlight with Hansa Rostock, before eventually earning a move to Rangers just under 12 months ago for an initial fee of £4.3 million, which could eventually rise to £5.2 million.

In 17 appearances across all competitions this season, Naderi has scored nine and assisted six, battling with Kevin Kelsy, Lawrence Shankland, and Bojan Miovksi for a starting berth at Ibrox with Youssef Chermiti out with a long-term injury.

TEAMtalk reports, however, that Rangers have no intention of allowing Naderi to go anywhere anytime soon, as West Ham and Wolves will have to pay a sizeable chunk to lure him south of the border this winter - a clear stumbling block for both.

West Ham can boast each of Joel Piroe, Taty Castellanos, and Pablo Felipe as their centre-forward options right now, but despite their obvious quality, recently appointed head coach Scott Parker doesn't appear to be convinced by any of them.

The former Burnley boss will be looking to stamp his authority on the Hammers squad this January, and a move for the six-foot-four-inch Naderi poses an attractive option for Parker, who must expect to face strong stubbornness from Rangers in their pursuit.

Wolves, meanwhile, have each of Raul Jimenez, Adam Armstrong, and Sean Neave as options up top, though with Jimenez injured and not getting any younger, Armstrong struggling, and Neave not yet fully trusted, Naderi has been outlined as a candidate that the Black Country outfit could target.

Naderi's natural physicality and goalscoring ability have surely put him on the radar of numerous clubs across Europe, as well as West Ham and Wolves, who must be prepared to splash the cash if they are to lure him to England in the next couple of months.

What do you make of the links to Ryan Naderi? Would you like to see him at your club? How much would you be willing to spend on him? Share your thoughts below!

Scott Parker didn't get the dream start he'd hoped for at West Ham after replacing Nuno Espírito Santo at the helm, losing 2-1 at Ewood Park to Blackburn Rovers.

With three Championship promotions on his CV, the former England midfielder knows exactly what it takes to guide a club out of this division, and is expected to be backed in January with automatic promotion in his sights.

Cesar Peixoto, meanwhile, will be intent on guiding Wolves back to the Premier League at the first opportunity after succeeding Rob Edwards at Molineux in the summer, and seems to be looking for that added spark up top in Naderi.

Whether either of them will be able to lure Naderi to England remains to be seen, though both of their aims have been made abundantly clear.

#2134. Official: Starting XIs for Genoa vs. AC Milan – five changes from Ferencvaros defeat

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim has named his starting line-up for the game against Genoa, and the big names are back.

Having been comfortably beaten by Ferencvaros in midweek, the pressure is on Milan and Amorim to deliver against a resurgent Genoa. It is a familiar feeling, given the derby became a must-win after the Bologna defeat, and the Udinese victory was after the Bournemouth debacle.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The task is not made easier by the list of injuries. Pietro Terracciano, Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Alexis Saelemaekers, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze and Strahinja Pavlovic are all out, with all of them long-term issues barring the Serbian centre-back.

Amorim has opted to go with a three-man defence composed of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter and Sankhoun Diawara ahead of the goalkeeper and captain Mike Maignan, who returns having served his Europa League suspension on Thursday.

The midfield engine room will feature Adrien Rabiot and Luka Modric in the double pivot, with Yunus Musah the right wing-back and Diego Moreira on the other side. Christian Pulisic and Alphadjo Cisse will play as attacking midfielders, with Gonçalo Ramos leading the line.

The bench is made up of mostly Milan Futuro players again given the aforementioned injury woes, though Davide Bartesaghi, Ardon Jashari, Omari Hutchinson and Francesco Camarda are waiting in the wings.

Official Milan XI (3-4-2-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara; Musah, Rabiot, Modric, Moreira; Pulisic, Cisse; Ramos.

#2133. Derby County release exciting Eiran Cashin update

Derby County have confirmed that Eiran Cashin is back in training, with the defender in line to feature for John Eustace’s side after the international break.

The Rams have endured a miserable campaign so far, and even though they beat Bolton last time out, they are 23rd in the Championship, having won just twice all season, and they are five points from safety.

So, it’s a concerning time to be a Derby fan, and Eustace has understandably come in for fierce criticism at times.

However, the one major mitigating factor in Eustace’s favour has been the number of injuries that Derby have suffered.

The Rams chief has had to do without a number of important players throughout the season so far, particularly in defence, with Cashin, Sondre Langås, Matt Clarke, Charlie Taylor and Derry Murkin among the absentees.

That forced Derby into the free agent market, with Jack Robinson and Shane Duffy joining to bolster the ranks.

And, whilst the duo played their part in the win over Bolton, with Robinson getting on the scoresheet, Eustace will be desperate to get his first-team players back out on the pitch as soon as possible.

Find out which Championship team takes top spot for the highest house prices around their stadium from 2026 figures.

Pleasingly for the Rams, there has been some positive news on the injury front, as the club shared a social media post of Cashin back with the group.

The 25-year-old, who returned to Pride Park on loan from Brighton in the summer, has not played since the 2-1 defeat at home to Birmingham City in September due to a calf injury.

That has kept the Irish international out of action for two months, but he is now back training with his teammates, which is a massive boost for Eustace.

Therefore, provided he doesn’t suffer any setbacks, it seems highly likely that Cashin will be in the starting XI when Derby return to action at Southampton on November 21.

This season has been a real struggle for Derby fans, and with away games at Southampton, Wolves and Middlesbrough in the next four games, there may be some more difficult days ahead for the Rams.

But, it’s important to recognise how injuries have impacted the club, as Eustace has been robbed of so many key players, especially at the back.

Of course, that doesn’t absolve him of all blame, but it’s needed to add context around Derby’s situation.

So, all connected to the East Midlands outfit will be delighted to see Cashin back involved, and they will expect the centre-back to be an influential figure very quickly.

That was reflected with these supporters, who clearly feel Cashin will make a big impact on the team...

Meanwhile, these fans were delighted to hear something positive after months of negativity around the club.

#2132. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

#2131. Milan Primavera 5-1 AlbinoLeffe: Vincent Ibrahimovic scores twice in second consecutive rout

On a day in which Milan’s first team, Futuro and Primavera sides all play, things have started on the right note.

After a tough run of recent results in the league, the Primavera managed to build on their mid-week cup win with a strong performance against last weekend Monza, winning 5-0 away from home. Max Anastasio, Mattia Zaramella (x2), Riccardo Grassini and Yanis Messaoudi scored in that rout.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, returning home to the PUMA House of Football, the challenge was to build on that result. The response was resounding: Giovanni Renna’s side won 5-1 against AlbinoLeffe in the early kick-off.

Milan took the lead after five minutes with a fine goal from Balentien, and the second goal came in the tenth minute through Vincent Ibrahimovic, who capitalized on a defensive error.

The visitors pulled one back in the 30th minute through Gamba, but in the 36th minute the Rossoneri reopened their two-goal advantage as Ibrahimovic got his name on the scoresheet again, curling one around the goalkeeper from inside the box.

In the second half, Anastasio scored the fourth goal on the hour mark following a cross from Angelicchio, and in the 68th minute Zaramella sealed the deal with an easy one-on-one with the goalkeeper.

The win puts Milan in sixth place in the table on 16 points, and they are now just five points off Parma in top spot, and three behind both Roma and Inter who occupy second and third at the moment. Next up is a trip to face Lazio after the break, the team currently in the place above them.

#2130. Leeds United ace Dan James 'would be an incredible signing for Sheffield United' in January

Sheffield United have been urged to make a move for one of Leeds United's players in the January transfer window, with Chris Wilder's side lacking width and creativity.

Following the exits of Gus Hamer, Callum O'Hare, and Andre Brooks, Sheffield United were left short of those profiles. Ben Brereton-Diaz and Romelle Donovan were brought in on loan but bolstering that area could make the difference in January.

Sheffield United have scored the 15th-most goals in the division from the 16th-most xG (FotMob), which will have to improve if they are to make the top eight under Chris Wilder, but a Leeds United fan favourite could perhaps be the answer to their problems.

FLW’s Sheffield United fan pundit Jimmy was asked about the fact the January transfer window is fast approaching. We asked him to name one player that he'd absolutely love his club to make a move for, while keeping it realistic but also being free to be ambitious as well.

He answered with a player who has torn up the Championship in recent years, saying: "I know we have talked about [Ryan] Kavuma-McQueen.

"But in a similar vein, I think that probably one of the more ambitious signings that Sheffield United could realistically look at is Dan James at Leeds United.

"Donovan is currently playing on the left-hand side and doing a good job. He can't play on the right.

"But another man who can play right or left, and probably leans more towards the right, is Dan James at Leeds.

The 25 top scorers in the Championship since the second tier was rebranded back in 2004/05, including Billy Sharp and Aleksandar Mitrovic.

"I think it would be an incredible signing for Sheffield United. And he'd be a game-changer, really.

"Somebody that would transform our fortunes and possibly our chances of making the play-offs and having a real go this season.

"I think it would be a coup. I know it's another Leeds player, which, you know, there is some ridicule between the fanbases about that.

"But, ultimately, if he improves our first 11? Get him in."

Sheffield United were already lacking genuine pace in their squad, but that problem has only been exacerbated by Femi Seriki's injury, which will rule arguably their quickest player out for the remainder of the 2026/27 season.

Speed in the wide areas is something the Blades desperately need more of, particularly when looking to stretch opposition defences and carry a greater threat in transition. However, pace is not their only shortcoming, with creativity and firepower also in relatively short supply.

Bringing in somebody who can offer at least some of all three attributes should therefore be a January priority. James would be an excellent option, with his explosive speed, directness, and goalscoring instincts potentially addressing several of Sheffield United's biggest attacking weaknesses.

It may be an ambitious move for Sheffield United to pull off, but it is certainly not unrealistic. James will have two years remaining on his Leeds contract this coming summer, has recently turned 29, and has slipped down the pecking order somewhat at Elland Road due to the form of Noah Okafor and the signing of Harry Wilson over the summer.

That combination could make him an obvious candidate for Leeds to offload, particularly if they feel they can reinvest his wages or any transfer fee elsewhere in their squad. There is definitely a chance he available this January, which will definitely be of interest to Championship sides.

James is arguably one of those classic players who is too good for the Championship but has never quite been able to establish himself as a consistent Premier League performer. He has 29 goals and 25 assists in 109 Championship appearances, compared to 12 goals and 13 assists across 129 Premier League outings.

#2129. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”
