#2078. West Ham Insider Reveals Recruitment Mess Behind Club’s Decline

West Ham United are still suffering because of years of bad recruitment, Claret & Hugh has been told by a Hammers insider today. The source, who did not wish to be named, described the situation as a mess and laid the blame for the club’s current predicament firmly and squarely at muddled, poor recruitment.

Speaking to Claret & Hugh, the source said:

“It’s all down to recruitment and it’s been bad, a real mess.”

“It’s a hodge podge with players being brought from everywhere by loads of different people. We’re years behind and needed a complete reset, we had to start again and consider how we recruit.”

Honest words, and not ones that many West Ham fans would disagree with. The club has spent years changing managers, recruitment chiefs and transfer strategies, seemingly without allowing any one approach enough time to work. The result is a squad assembled under several different regimes, with little evidence of a consistent long-term plan.

It has always been Daniel Křetínský’s wish at West Ham to have a director of football in charge, and whilst we don’t have that exact job title at the club currently, Nils Koppen, as Director of Player Recruitment, is as good as a director of football in all but name.

What is clear is that the club are going to have to rebuild the recruitment structure brick by brick. And it’s worth pointing out that even as recently as the summer, there was still something of a mix-up, with a blend of recruitment ideas and Nuno Espírito Santo being allowed to bring in three players in Joël Piroe, Manor Solomon and Morato.

Kretinsky is a big believer in the structured recruitment model

That is hardly the definition of a joined-up recruitment strategy, although it’s also important to recognise that Koppen arrived with very little time to prepare for the summer window. The bigger issue is whether West Ham are finally prepared to commit to a consistent approach rather than changing direction whenever the manager changes.

We’re semi-lucky in one respect because we do have another transfer window coming up in January, giving Koppen and Scott Parker an opportunity to address some of the more obvious problems within the squad.

But this is definitely a time when West Ham have to commit to a transfer policy and allow it to play out and bear fruit over a number of seasons. Toying with an approach and then giving up, as we did with both Tim Steidten and Kyle Macaulay, is precisely the sort of short-term thinking that has contributed to the problem.

The club cannot keep appointing recruitment specialists, allowing them to start rebuilding the squad and then abandoning the entire project when results turn sour. At some point, West Ham have to decide what sort of players they want, how they’re going to identify them and who is ultimately responsible for bringing them in.

January offers an opportunity to begin correcting some of the mistakes, but the problems described by our source won’t be fixed in a single transfer window. If West Ham are genuinely years behind in their recruitment, the rebuild needs to be given the time and consistency that previous attempts have lacked.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Where’s all this money coming from to fund the (start of) this overhaul. I can’t recall all the figures now but debt in excess of £200m, some of which had to (and has been) repaid, losing £100m a year and whilst wages have reduced by, say 50%, so has revenue. Unless Kretinsky is now a 45% and the major shareholder ( there appears to be conflicting info as to whether this transaction has completed) he is, based on history, little chance of him providing a transfer kitty and even if he is how does ‘FFP’ come into the equation?

I don’t think we needed a club insider to tell us about this issue. Yes not all signings will work out, but our success rate has been particularly poor in the last 3 years. I am not against a manager making suggestions as you allude to with Nuno, but they must be agreed by all relevant parties, then it becomes a cooperative relationship between manager and DOF.

The issue is that poor recruitment rarely costs directly on the books. Players amortise and those that don’t work out at all go out on loan bringing in loan fees.

The real problem lies in the contributions that they do not make. We invest and don’t lose out on the books but we do lose out in having invested in a player who did not contribute for us.

That affects results so affects success so affects us financially in that respect. Repeated poor investments.

We had it all then. We needed to continue with the Jarrod Bowen type of recruitment. We needed to back the manager and his coaching staff.

Instead, we were treated to exotic ideas of radical change which turned out to be a waste of money, time and a football club.

Tim Steidten could not believe his luck and bank balance as he scoured the world for excuses to spend on as high a profile as possible players to add to and become the basis of his team. No thoughts as to how these players would work in the game plans with the other players we already had. Only a passing reference to the team coach as the stars were aligned. The manager’s fault when success on the field was not forthcoming.

Poor recruitment played its part but continuity and investment in building upon a solid foundation was the real problem.

Let us hope that Scott Parker is allowed to continue to build our new team and not just until a more exotic name like Pellegrini or Lopetegui gets whispered into the ears of Daniel Kretinsky.

We have an opportunity now. We must take it.

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

#2075. West Ham Exclusive: Hammers Open To Castellanos Sale As Koppen Targets Striker

Claret & Hugh can exclusively reveal today that West Ham United are exploring the possibility of selling striker Taty Castellanos during the January transfer window. However, the chances of Everton returning for the Argentine have been described as “unlikely” by a football agent speaking to C&H.

Everton were reported to have made a deadline-day bid at the end of the summer transfer window, but with West Ham unable to source a replacement in time, the offer was rejected. The Premier League club’s interest was substantial, although there is currently no indication that David Moyes will renew his pursuit.

It would be fair to say that Castellanos has been something of a disappointment in the Championship this season, and West Ham are now actively looking to recruit another forward when the window opens in January. Director of Player Recruitment Nils Koppen has already begun making enquiries to agents and clubs as the Hammers prepare to strengthen Scott Parker’s squad.

Koppen wants to sign a striker in January

Speaking to Claret & Hugh this morning, our source confirmed that the club’s search for a new centre-forward is already underway.

“Nils has already made an approach for one striker in France.”

When asked whether there could also be departures from West Ham’s attacking department, the agent added:

“West Ham would sell Castellanos if an offer came in.”

The source did not specify how much West Ham would require for the Argentine, nor did they identify the striker Koppen has approached. However, the comments suggest that the club are prepared to consider a significant change to their attacking options in January.

Castellanos cost West Ham £27 million when he arrived from Lazio in January, but his performances in the Championship have fallen well short of expectations. The striker’s difficulties have been evident throughout the campaign, with his lack of goals already raising serious questions about his future.

Everton’s previous interest was first reported in September, when it emerged that West Ham had been prepared to consider a substantial offer but could not find a suitable replacement before the deadline.

The possibility of a January departure has also been discussed previously, although today’s information provides a fresh indication that the club are actively exploring their options.

It will come as little surprise to anybody who has watched Castellanos this season that West Ham would consider moving him on. The Argentine has struggled to make the impact expected of a £27 million striker, and Parker is now beginning the process of assessing what he needs from his squad.

Whether a suitable offer arrives remains to be seen, particularly with a return from Everton considered unlikely by our source. But with Koppen already approaching potential replacements, it appears West Ham are preparing for the possibility of a significant change up front when the January window opens.

#2074. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#2073. Arsenal transfer interest faces major obstacle as Santos secure £83m teenage talent

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal may have to rethink their interest in Santos forward Ignacio Pereira after the Brazilian club secured the teenager’s future with a substantial release clause.

The 16-year-old has caught the eye of a number of European clubs after an impressive campaign in Santos’ youth teams. The likes of Arsenal are said to have been watching his progress.

However, Santos have acted swiftly to secure the services of one of their most exciting young talents. Pereira signed his first professional contract with the club on November 4, tying him to the club until December 2029.

The deal also includes a 100 million euro release clause (around £83.4 million), according to Brazilian journalist Bruno Lima from UOL.

This poses a major problem for Arsenal if they are looking to sign the Argentine but also offers a lot of security for Santos, as they want to develop him as a first-team player.

Pereira has signed a new deal amid increasing interest in his development. Reports in Brazil have previously said that Arsenal, Real Betis, AC Milan, Lille, Standard Liège and Zenit are all keeping an eye on the rising star.

The club have now secured his services for another three years. The new agreement was awaiting registration with the Brazilian Football Confederation when the details emerged.

Pereira has spent three years at Santos, having joined from Juventude in 2023. He previously developed at Grêmio before moving to the São Paulo club.

Pereira has certainly lived up to the expectations. He scored an impressive 6 goals in 17 games in the Brazilian Under-17 Championship, making him the second-highest scorer for Santos. He also scored 4 goals in the Paulista Under-17 Championship.

This is very promising. It is his first season playing at under-17 level.

Pereira has been compared to Julián Álvarez due to his mobility and ability to play outside the box.

But the youngster cites another big name up front as his main inspiration. According to UOL, he cites Manchester City’s Erling Haaland as his inspiration, while Lionel Messi is still his football idol.

His profile suggests a versatile number nine who can play lower down the pitch, be an attacking midfielder and play with another striker. He has impressed the youth coaches at Santos with his finishing ability, physicality and desire to win.

He has a long way to go. Reports from Brazil suggest that Santos want to improve his tactical awareness and behaviour before making him more responsible.

He is being considered by the club for inclusion in their squad for the 2027 Copa São Paulo de Futebol Júnior (known as Copinha) and could start on the bench.

This interest from Arsenal does not necessarily mean that there is an imminent move for Pereira. The player is only 16, and a potential deal is made much more complicated due to a new contract.

Maybe the best course of action for Mikel Arteta’s recruitment team is to keep an eye on him. Santos has made it clear where they stand, and Pereira can now work towards his dream. Being in their first team.

#2072. Player Ratings: Genoa 1-2 AC Milan – De Winter, Pulisic and Rabiot take charge

AC Milan responded to the criticism with an important win at Genoa on Sunday afternoon. A few players made the difference and below are the ratings for the Rossoneri.

After the mid-week failure against Ferencvaros, Milan knew that three points were more or less a must against Genoa. Thankfully, aside from a dramatic ending, it was a comfortable game for the Rossoneri and a few of the players also got to send some strong signals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

👎 Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

👔 Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

Maignan (6.5): We saw a couple of good stops from him, including one on Vitinha in the second half, and his distribution was decent. He couldn’t really do anything about the goal either, as it was a really good effort from Ellertsson.

Gila (6): I liked his performance overall but there were a couple of moments that dragged down the rating for me, more specifically the fouls he committed. Put simply, he was a bit too rash and it was after one of the free-kicks he caused that Genoa scored their goal.

De Winter (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Diawara (6): He was carded for a very rash challenge, but apart from that, he kept his calm at the back and had decent positioning throughout. It’s not like Genoa threatened Milan a lot, but enough for a pass here still.

Moreira (6.5): It was a lively start from him, I would say, with some good moments on that right flank. However, the end product wasn’t always amazing (some blocked shots), and he faded a bit attacking-wise as the game went on. Solid though and he did put in a defensive shift at the end.

Modric (7): We got to see some really nice flicks and quick play from him today. Defensively, he contributed as well, which was especially clear with a last-ditch toe-poke to avoid a 1v1 for Genoa. There was one poor pass into the middle which could have proved costly, but the rest was good.

Rabiot (7.5): He was back to his usual self today after what was a subpar display against Ferencvaros. Great movement between the lines and elegance on the ball were his main strengths, also getting the assist for the opener.

Musah (6): We have to praise him for doing well in a ‘new’ position, following the instructions from Amorim nearly perfectly. What stopped him from getting a higher rating here was the big giveaway at the end, which Genoa really should have done more with.

Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

Cisse (7): It was a very tidy finish to give Milan the lead, showing once again that he knows how to turn up in the right place at the right time. However, for a higher rating, I would have liked to see more in his 1v1s, which weren’t always so successful.

Ramos (5.5): I’m torn here. It was unselfish to pass to Pulisic for the second goal rather than shooting himself, so that deserves praise. However, I actually think he was very sloppy in open play with heavy touches and positioning that sometimes left a lot to be desired. I suppose the big question is how much his defensive work rate is worth to the rating.

Terracciano (6): Surprisingly good! He had a crucial deflection on a shot from El Shaarawy and also headed the ball away quite a few times in the end, certainly contributing to the three points.

Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

Jashari (6): We didn’t see much in terms of attacking contributions and build-up, since he came on with ten minutes to go, but he was responsible for a few clearances at the end.

Estupinan (5.5): I don’t think it was much of a foul, but in those moments, you shouldn’t even give the referee the opportunity to blow the whistle. He knows that.

Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

There are a lot of nuances, which you aren’t picking up on apparently.

Name me 5 instances of service that he received that he didn’t score from? i’m struggling to recall five all season. He feeds on scraps. He gets no decent service. He has to play as an AM just to help create something. And even though we didn’t bring him in to pull defenders for others to score, he is at least doing that.

You have to take his performances with a grain of salt.

Herean instance for you. Why did he pass it to Pulisic instead of shooting? A true striker buries that opportunity without even thinking. He is a PSG sub and a tap in merchant. I am sorry.

Spot on again. Lack of service is a Milan way of life. It’s probably because the supporting cast has always been hell bent on trying to score. Leao, Pulisic, and now Moreira, Hutchinson and Cisse are players who look to score first, not to assist.

I think in that specific instance, the extra pass was the right choice. He’s putting a man in a better position to score. In fact, I think Pulisic should have ideally let the ball run to Moreira, who would have had better angles with his left foot. Another example of Pulisic being laser focused on trying to score, as I mention above, and similar to his clash with Bartesaghi, but at least in this case you could say that Puli was in front of Moreira and thus did not really see him, as opposed to the Bartesaghi incided when Pulisic was behind him and should have deferred to Bartesaghi.

@VERO Who cares who scores as long as they are scoring? Ramos could’ve shot the ball there, most strikers would have, but he made the right play. Pulisic was in better position to score. Assist is just as good in that case. It shows a good team mentality. He could’ve been selfish, especially with all the noise he’s getting about not scoring goals but he still made the best play for the team. He should get credit for that. And this idea that Pulisic should’ve let the ball run to Moreira but is too “laser focused on goals is absolutely absurd. He was in the best position to score. Period. Not to mention he has no clue that Moreira is even running in behind him there.

You can’t win with with this site. If you don’t score people complain, if you score people complain that you are too “laser focused on goals.” People just love to complain.

Re-read my post. We’re saying the same thing vis-a-vis Ramos. I’m not one of the ones who is against him. I think maybe we overpaid, but as it stand I think he’s doing alright overall, and I think he’ll eventually start scoring.

As to Puli and Moreira, I’m nitpicking! Chill. Glad the ball ended up in the back of the net.

I guess this is going to be our status quo. Some good games or half good games, and some horrible ones (especially in the Europa League). Overall, I thought we started a bit poorly in the first 5 minutes or so, then completely took control of the game and scored to then stopping playing football by minute 30. I thought this is also a tale of 2 flanks, the right flank with Pulišić and Moreira & sometimes Gila stepping up was terrific while the left flank with Musah, Cissé é Diwarara looked a bit dodgy offensively. I don’t know what to think of this formula overall, but knowing Amorim, I won’t surprised if he tries yet another tactic with Ramos as an AM, Gila as a midfielder,… with him you can’t be sure. Maignan: Overall he was there when needed, and I don’t think he can be blamed for that shot from way out. Musah: I almost pity the guy. He started looking a bit decent in the midfield, then Amorim throws him as a RB for one game, then as a LB in the next. But I think it mostly shows how little confidence Amorim has in Bartesaghi & Estupiñán, which to be fair, is understandable. / Estupiñán: came in late and caused a foul that almost gave away a draw, such an Estupiñán thing to do… Diawara: Still a bit raw and rough around the edges, but overall I did like his efforts. Terracciano: we actually survived having him, Musah as LB then Estupiñán on the pitch… he wasn’t so bad this time apart from a horrible pass. Which makes me thing maybe against Bologna, we should REALLY have subbed him in instead of having Musah on the flank and weakening the midfield… but the past is the past. De Winter: I wasn’t actually super impressed by him. Almost gave away a goal one minute in and managed to make Vitinha look like Vitinha sometimes, but then again considering how much Gila steps up, I guess he can be a bit overloaded. Gila: I don’t like him leaving too much gap behind, but honestly his attacks look more polished than Pavlović’s. Moreira: not that good defensively, but offensively, my man is a demon. Modrić: Honestly, I think the recent adjustments of Amorim (or whatever one can call them), suit him a bit better. He looked more rejuvinated recently. Rabiot: some check if he has a knife, because he was tearing through Genoa’s midfield like butter. Cissé: his speed is a liability for sure, but this kid sure knows how to make himself available. Pulišić: his best game in a while IMO, he scored, pressed like there is no tomorrow, helped in the defense, won duels,… Ramos: the simple fact that in that position in that moment, he chose to set up Pulišić instead of trying to score himself from what was already a closed angle, is a positive. Overall, we’re 5 points from first place, which ain’t bad and I’m assuming inter is going to tear through Como as usual so we might be fourth. Let’s now hope the dreaded international break won’t claim any more victims from our side…

The more I rewatch these matches, the more I see players constantly staring at each other and pointing. Nobody has any idea where the others are going to be. In my head, this is about 70% ownership constantly turning over a significant portion of the squad every year and 30% management for constantly tinkering with the lineups so nobody can settle into a rhythm. Everyone get together and finally get things right to allow a little stability!

“which ain’t bad and I’m assuming inter is going to tear through Como as usual so we might be fourth.” Damn, I was hoping not to nail that one, but I unfortunately did.

Inter will walk to the Title. I expect ny January they will have 10 point lead already.

They will do so in spite of Chivu, from muscle memory on the back of what Inzaghi had built. But that won’t matter.

Don’t sleep on Roma. They’re looking very strong this year, and recently seem to be hitting stride. The title might not be decided until Inter-Roma on April 11.

I know we won, but taking our foot off the gas at minute 30 up only 2 shows the same problem as losing on Thursday. We don’t have the killing instinct.

60 min of Allegriball today makes me realize just how bad these injuries are. I can almost hear Amorim telling the guys to slow it down and conserve.

Look, Cisse is really good at taking his chances. That said his movement as part of the team is poor. I don’t see him as a 1v1 player. That said if he moves the ball quicker with his strong hold up play and learns to make the right runs he will be a very good player. What I did like about today was how the goals were scored by players working together. I’m tired of hero ball. ACM has no superstars, but they have some very good players and players with potential. I don’t think there was a motm, if there was it was Mike.

If it weren’t for the fact that Amorim pushed so hard to waste €74 million on him, it’s clear that Ramos should be benched and replaced by Cisse. Cisse’s natural talent for being in the right place at the right time and being able to get off really superb shots on goal, and to hold up the ball, qualify him as a natural 9, not a winger. As you said he lacks the speed and vision to pass to team mates to be a really good winger and playmaker. Amorim just can’t give up on the idea of benching his main guy Ramos for this young kid.

That’s a very limited observation. Cisse benefits from Ramos pulling defenders away and he doesn’t play where Ramos does, otherwise he’d get swallowed up by any decent CB. He benefits coming in from the flank, making late runs in and benefits from the defenders having been pulled out of position, like it happened today.

but yea, go ahead and play Cisse as a sole striker, see how it plays out.

We dont need $75M to make runs for others. His main job is to score. His “assist ” to Pulisic is a perfect example. It wasn’t a tap in for Pulisic and I actually thought he was going to miss it.

Instead Ramos could have hit the goal from you know…6 meters away. Easily. He is so bad that he couldn’t.

He’s just young and needs to know what he is going to do with the ball before he gets it. Yes, he has goals and his finishing has been top notched. But to really improve he has to see other players, understand what runs to make, and be faster on the ball. I am just reacting to some of the over the top evals. Let’s be clear, ACM has no superstars so let’s start looking at how they play together as a unit.

Let’s not forget we have a ton of players still injured and the subs really show that. Terracciano actually played pretty well but the rest just put the match at risk. Hutch can’t be worth 40 mil so he’ll be going back. Pervis… nothing needs to be said lol. Jashari is not looking like he’s the solution there. The rest of the team showed heart and grit so very happy with that. De Winter had one of his mountain top matches if only he could turn those peaks in to plateaus then we may not need to spend big on a “center” CB. Puli, Rabiot, Moreira, Cisse, just excellent as usual. Ramos… I’ve said what I need to say about him, not much has changed. This is not the role or team OR league for him. Really need the injured to come back and we can start to actually finish games comfortably. Great team win in a difficult atmosphere!

I will say that Ramos’s assist is appreciated and a striker with more confidence would shoot there 9 times out of 10. However, he barely got it off and Pulisic had to do a lot to make that a goal. I understand Amorim saying our play style needs to support Ramos more but if we’re talking about using Ramos as a garbage goal kind of striker where he’s playing mostly in the 6 yard box etc, then that may take years lol. In all the hold up play and everything else that goes into a good striker, I don’t see it. He wants to play slightly behind or off the shoulder of the defenders but to do that we would need to totally change our style of play. Right now he has to play in front of the defense and he just looks like a fish out of water in that area. Overall very happy with the team and Ramos shows a lot of heart but I still don’t think this is ultimately the place for him.

I am growing concerned about Ramos. No scores, 1 assist (today to CP). When will he begin to step up?

As usual, CP is targeted and on his butt over and over. Why do the refs allow this?

No scores is worrying but so are the turnovers that no one talked about.

I remember all summer long we were reading what was Amorim point percentage per game at United and how with the same team Carrick would have won the title if Amorim was fired earlier, don’t look now, but United might get relegated if they don’t fire Carrick. They are 19th on the table with only a better goal difference that keeps them from being last. Another great win by Milan. Keep stacking wins.

I honestly don’t put too much stock into what any coach does at Man U, Chelsea or Milan (sadly). Those clubs have all been run so poorly for an extended period of time that there is only so much a coach can do there.

Tbf Ramos participated well in the Cisse’s goal. He distracted two defenders and both of them followed him to nowhere and left Cisse alone lmao. But Ramos’s positioning still amazes me. It is like he doesn’t have any goal instincts. How is that guy a CF?

Well, the second defender was at fault there. Great move by Ramos but the defender behind actually sees that he was blocked by the first one. He could have stayed for Cisse. That was bad defending for sure.

Spot on. But now let’s just say Ramos has distracted the opponent defenders for Cisse to score. So then what? Who’s not able to run to the opposite end of where to score a goal yourself? This I get a smart striker occasionally does but this guy never does any other runs. This quality of creating space for others to score is one I’ll never get. The same was said about Leao too when nothing else was working for him.

Absolutely! I remember they were saying the same thing for Gimenez too. Literally the same thing..they were saying “he contributes, it is more than just goals” etc. And Ramos pass to Pulisic was terrible. He is lucky Pulisic didnt miss it. It shouldn’t even count as assist.

This is probably the last game to give Camarda an idea on what Amorim’s plans for him are. Up 2-0 he still couldn’t get anytime. He simply wants his $75M friend to score one. Desperate. Camarda should leave for his own good and career.

A few thoughts Positives 1. This was a really good win. We played an inform team in front of a loud crowd and came out swinging. There were some nerves with this one but a 2-1 win is a great result. 2. The Genoa goalie made no good saves. Mike made 3-4. He really is a world class guy 3. Ramos had a hand in both goals…he needs to score, but he was definitely a positive today 4. Cisse shows up in great spots and has a ton of confidence. Am I the only one who thinks he should be a striker? He has a poachers mentality, presses well and has good hold up play. He is not great in the build up or tracking back….so I’d love for him to get a few games up top. 5. Pulisic, Rabiot, and Modric….so smart and always moving into good positions without the ball. It helped keep that lead. Negatives 1. How long do we have to wait for Milan to be a team where most of the players have good vision? Musah, Cisse, Jashari, Hutchison, Moreira, Pavlović no one sees the pitch well. 2. Our depth sucks. As soon as the subs came on, our level of play fell apart. 3. If you are going to allow physical play, the ref cannot call that foul on Estupian. Such garbage

Amorim must know by now that rotating 5-6 players each match will lead to inconsistency and will ultimately get him fired. Today was a win with the right players on the pitch. And the right players in the stands.

From October 11th up until today, November 8th, Milan played 9 games in 28 days. Let that sink in before you try to complain about rotations. Also, outside of Torriani and Bartesaghi all other players that played vs Ferencvaros played today. He has no choice but to rotate and use the same players because that’s all he has at his disposal because of injuries and lack of depth.

“Torriani and Bartesaghi all other players that played vs Ferencvaros played today.”

So that means he didnt rotate against Ferencvaros? Which is worse because that means he threw that game away by his horrible tactics.

He rotate the starters so they can get some rest. Did you watch the 2 games? What do tactics have to do if the other teams players play harder than Milan players? What does tactics have to do when Milan players pass to the wrong team, or cant make a simple pass forward? When Musah today lost the ball that led to a Genoa chance and Mike saved, was that due tactics or individual mistakes? At the end of the day, the players play on the pitch, not the coach. The coach can have the perfect tactics but if players make individual mistakes or fail to execute the tactics how is that poor tactics?

Important victory ✌️❤️🖤 Now the Germans are coming, so hopefully they will start cleaning the team of trash like El Stupido, Shіtshari, Camarda and always injured parasites like Loftus Merdus Chick, Chukweze and Salamaker!

If we are being honest, Milan’s two goals were ‘freak’ goals. On the first goal, Pulisic won the ball back on his own, then Ramos made a nice decoy run to open up space for Cisse. The second goal was a gift from Genoa. Milan’s offense created nothing the entire game.

Happy Ramos got an assist cuz he was vital to both goals, so often he makes the decoy run to open space for the 2nd runner. With better service he’d score plenty himself, but we dont create many good chances at all. Terra also did much better today, definitely crucial to keeping the 3 points.

I feel bad for Jashari cuz on their goal hes literally the ONLY one trying to close anyone down,everyone else just stands off and let’s him shoot… we really need someone who can create more clear cut chances for the forward line cuz we simply do not create enough clear cut opportunities, so many come down to the other side making an error themselves. Glad we scraped the 2 points out today at least

I hope in the next game Milan don’t rotate heavily….maybe 1 or 2 changes max. Otherwise next game it won’t be consistent again. You just have to stick with same players to gel up.

Milan exaggeration in playing in the back almost lost them the game. I dont understand why its so difficult for Milan in the last decade to build quick attacks. Nonetheless, 3 points earned. I hope the manager can fix these observations and realize the fans like a fierce Milan.

#2071. Arsenal handed William Saliba boost as Arteta considers defender’s return

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

The William Saliba Arsenal boost comes at a crucial time. Saliba can use the November international break to build up his fitness after missing out on France’s latest squad.

Arteta confirmed that the defender had returned to full training ahead of Arsenal’s Champions League meeting with Slavia Prague. He also completed 45 minutes in a behind-closed-doors-friendly last week as he stepped up his recovery.

However, Saliba did not feature in the 2-1 victory. Arteta included him in the matchday squad for the first time this season, but the Frenchman remained an unused substitute.

It means he was not selected by Zinedine Zidane for France’s Nations League games against Italy and Turkey. This gives Arsenal a chance to continue working on his recovery. He will not be travelling for international games or playing in competitive matches.

Saliba has not featured since he suffered a back injury during France’s World Cup semi-final against Spain in July. Arteta has had to find alternatives in central defence in the early stages of the campaign.

Since transferring to Arsenal from Aston Villa in August, Konsa has played a part in filling the gap left by Saliba. His presence in the centre of defence complements Gabriel Magalhães and gives Arteta more options.

The England defender is also expected to be fit for the match against Hull City on Saturday. According to Arteta, the player’s replacement in the game against Slavia Prague was just a precaution after he reported some discomfort.

The fact that he has made a recovery means that Arsenal have the option to control how Saliba returns. Arteta has the possibility of bringing Saliba back gradually, as Konsa is ready to play and Mosquera is also available.

But Saliba’s return still matters. He needs to get back in shape before the fixtures start getting tougher after the international break.

Arteta has made it clear he will respect whatever decision Zidane makes regarding Saliba’s availability but acknowledges that he needs some game time after being out for so long.

France will play Italy on November 12 and then Turkey three days later. This means Saliba will be missing those matches, as Zidane named his 23-man squad on Friday.

This means he will be able to continue to be monitored by the club at their London Colney training ground. He won’t be able to return to play in international games ahead of his first appearance for the club.

Arsenal will be hoping that he can use the extra time to get himself ready for the next set of games, including a trip to Newcastle before playing Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City at home.

Arteta will be keen to have Saliba back in contention but will be focused on getting him back at the right time.

There is some immediate optimism on Konsa’s fitness for the game against Hull. But more importantly, Saliba has now progressed to a point where he can be included in the planning process.

#2070. Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal set January transfer priorities as Fabrizio Romano delivers Piero Hincapié update

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal transfer news, Arsenal could approach the January transfer window with a different focus after Fabrizio Romano revealed that Mikel Arteta has no intention of weakening his defensive options.

Piero Hincapié has been linked with a move to Barcelona. There have been reports that a deal could be done involving Alejandro Balde, but Romano expects the Ecuadorian to stay at Emirates Stadium.

Arsenal have been strengthening their defensive department under Arteta. Hincapié only made the switch permanently from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer after joining on loan.

Despite competition, the 24-year-old is a key player in Arteta’s plans. His versatility to play in either a centre back or left back role gives Arteta a valuable option.

However, we can also gain insight into where Arsenal should target their recruitment from Romano’s latest comments. Instead of changing their defensive options, it could be an opportunity to improve their attacking options.

Despite competition, the 24-year-old is a key player in Arteta’s plans. His versatility to play in either a centre back or left back role gives Arteta a valuable option.

However, we can also gain insight into where Arsenal should target their recruitment from Romano’s latest comments. Instead of changing their defensive options, it could be an opportunity to improve their attacking options.

However, Arsenal have little incentive to let him leave halfway through the season, as losing a two-in-one defender will cause problems for Arteta, given how much they need to do in multiple competitions.

Romano’s comments suggest that Arsenal are happy with their existing defensive unit and don’t want to cause any disruption to their balance. He also suggested that Hincapié is an important player for them, meaning he’s unlikely to leave in January.

That leaves Barcelona needing to explore alternative targets if they want to strengthen their backline. A deal involving Balde and Hincapié does not currently appear to be a realistic option.

The more interesting part of Romano’s report is Arsenal’s potential business at the other end of the field.

He feels they will be looking to make a move if the right attacking player comes up for grabs. But he doesn’t think they will make a signing just because they can in January.

This highlights the issues clubs face with mid-season transfers. Often selling clubs will be unwilling to lose key players, and finding suitable replacements can be tough.

As such, Arsenal are likely to look at the market to see what they can do. However, it looks like there could still be a forward brought in.

This is an important distinction. The point being made here is that whilst there is speculation around one particular player, Romano has indicated that Arsenal can strengthen their attacking options. This is not to say that any particular move is happening.

If Arteta keeps Hincapié, then Arsenal will maintain their defensive stability and possibly gain another option in attack.

Over the next few weeks we will get a better understanding of what is available to them. But for now it looks like Arsenal are not keen to lose Hincapié but will look to strengthen their attacking options if the right deal comes along.

#2069. £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

These remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

Not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined plan, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” said Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

For Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

De Zerbi said he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH

Newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA

Might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

There are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

At least the issues facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too big. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

“At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach said: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match plan at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

“We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc

"With the fans behind us, no one can stop us" 🖤Yoane Wissa reacts to Newcastle's win at Spurs! pic.twitter.com/itaiVO3Kx1

After a tumultuous summer, Jaissle has ushered in a new era of hope and positivity at Newcastle, with Wissa and Elanga reborn in attack.

"Oh Jaissle, I can boogie..." 🎶🕺 pic.twitter.com/FmvC2DrLMO

2 - Anthony Elanga is the first player to score in both of Newcastle United's first two Premier League games of a campaign since Alan Shearer in 2003-04.Footsteps. pic.twitter.com/VZ3hXEbpG7

2 - Tottenham Hotspur have lost their opening two matches of a league campaign without scoring for the first time since the 1974-75 season.Concerning. pic.twitter.com/N8izpVYslx

Jaissle records his first ever Premier League win, heaping more misery upon Tottenham, who begin the season with two defeats. Excellent second-half finishes from Elanga and Wissa have given the visitors a superb three points in the capital.

YOU MAGSSSS! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/PRM8yYg7Yl

Barnes attempts to latch onto a ball in behind, but Kinsky races out to claim. Spurs then almost half-heartedly come forward as Udogie tries to find Marmoush with a powerful cross. The new Spurs forward gets some contact on the ball, but it ricochets to Hall, who hacks it clear. Newcastle then make a late change as Toure replaces Barnes.

Fernandes clips a pinpoint cross into Marmoush. The Egyptian shoots via a first-time volley, but his tame attempt is easily gathered by Hornicek.

Van de Ven’s reintegration into Spurs’ defence hasn’t proved helpful. The hosts have been all at sea at the back since the restart. Newcastle showed little attacking ambition in the first half but have ripped Tottenham apart in the second.

Jaissle makes another double change as both goal-scorers, Elanga and Wissa, are taken off for Murphy and Ramsey. Elanga and Wissa have both produced extremely positive displays to kickstart their seasons under their new head coach.

Spurs have looked way off the pace in this second half and Newcastle are well worth their lead on the basis of their performance since the break.

The away fans sarcastically cheer as Tonali is withdrawn for Solanke. The former Newcastle midfielder has struggled against his old club, drastically failing to impact the game.

The visitors are in dreamland! Hall swings in a corner and Woltemade towers above Udogie to win the header. The ball breaks to Wissa, who fires a delightful acrobatic finish into the net, extending Newcastle’s advantage. Spurs’ crisis deepens. They’re on course for two defeats to start the season.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY

And this time it is another two of last summer’s signings who have combined for Newcastle United’s second goal of the afternoon.

Nick Woltemade won the initial header and got the assist a few seconds after replacing Joe Willock, but what a finish from Yoane Wissa, an improvised overhead flick from close range.

Newcastle needed Elanga and Wissa to be far better this season than they were in their first campaign on Tyneside and both of them have been electric so far under Matthias Jaissle.

As for Sandro Tonali, Newcastle saw this version of the Italy international all too often in his final season at St James’ Park. Good engine, runs around a lot, but does not influence the game in any meaningful way. A reminder Spurs spent £100m on him and have spent almost £400m in total this summer. They have been abject in the second half.

Porro tries his luck from range but Hornicek is there for Newcastle to tip the ball over the bar. The visitors then make a double change as Steur and Woltemade replace Nico and Willock.

De Zerbi makes a triple change as Spurs look to find a way back into this match. Robertson, Gray and Tel depart for Udogie, Moore and Kudus.

Spurs have a free kick in a dangerous position, but Tel slips as he goes to shoot and it flies well over the bar. That sums up Tottenham’s evening so far.

That makes two goals in two games for Elanga, who scored zero Premier League goals last season. It’s an outstanding finish, on the spin while falling backwards. It prompted some great noises from the away end, too, as the ball seemed to cross the line in slow motion.

The visitors have started his second half well and fly into the lead. Nico switches the play and picks out Dedic with a precise long-ball. The full-back cushions a header into Elanga, who swivels and slides a low effort in off the post to open the scoring and send the away support into a euphoric sea of celebration. What answers do Spurs and De Zerbi have now?

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm

Newcastle deserved that goal. They have been the stronger side since the halftime interval, and this is the Anthony Elanga that Eddie Howe thought he was signing last summer.

He scored on the opening weekend against Liverpool, but this was an even better finish, spinning sharply and sweeping a shot home on the turn. Smart dance moves for the celebration too.

It all came about from another long diagonal ball forward, but this time it was inch perfect from Nico Gonzalez for Harvey Barnes to put a header into the path of Elanga inside the box.

Newcastle are really growing into this contest, with Spurs getting deeper and deeper. Elanga is starting to get some joy out wide.

The momentum has arguably been with Newcastle since the interval. They’re pushing Spurs back towards their own goal. The visitors are waiting to fashion a real big chance.

Elanga latches onto Hall’s pass, gets in behind Spurs’ defence and beats Kinsky to the ball. However, it was a difficult pass to control and his touch is too heavy, causing the opportunity to disappear. Newcastle are certainly looking more adventurous at the start of this second half.

The visitors make a rare foray forward as Hall bends an ambitious curler from long range that flies off target. That is more encouraging for Newcastle.

Early drama at the start of this half as Spurs appeal for a penalty. Thiaw and Marmoush challenge for a 50-50. The Tottenham forward crashes to the floor as the Newcastle captain goes for the clearance. The referee’s on-field decision is no penalty and VAR agrees. After seeing the replays, there wasn’t too much contact and it would have been a harsh penalty if given.

We are back under way for the second half. Will we see a goal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium this evening?

Spurs have been knocking on the door and looked like the far more threatening side, but they’ve been unable to find an opening goal. Newcastle have defended diligently and frustrated their opponents. However, in forward areas, they look disjointed and are lacking serious firepower.

⏸️ @SpursOfficial 0-0 @NUFC There's nothing to separate the two sides at half-time pic.twitter.com/ICFqQ3eXMO

Tel has drifted out to the right wing and turns inside of Nico before whipping a ball into the box which narrowly evades Marmoush. Tonali then bursts forward and passes to Porro, but Hall thwarts Spurs’ latest attack by blocking the makeshift winger’s shot.

I would be worried if I were Matthias Jaissle. Newcastle have not looked comfortable dealing with Tottenham’s corners and goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek has made a couple of good saves this half to keep the scores level.

Much of Newcastle’s attacking play has been aimless, with long diagonal balls pumped forward that the Tottenham defence is prepared for and has tended to deal with easily.

Very little is happening in midfield and neither Joe Willock in the number 10 role nor Yoane Wissa at centre forward has had any real joy in the final third.

It all looks a bit predictable going forward and, if we are being ultra critical, a bit aimless too. They have not forced a save from the Spurs goalkeeper as we approach half time.

Marmoush has become far more involved over the last ten minutes and has showcased his quality with a few notable touches and darting runs. Nevertheless, Spurs have been unable to breach Newcastle’s stubborn defence.

A free-flowing Tottenham move involving Van Hecke and Marmoush ends with Porro sliding a low cross in towards the unmarked Tel at the back post. The Spaniard doesn’t quite can’t enough power on the delivery and Hornicek rushes out to collect.

Marmoush slips a clever pass through to Robertson, who fires in a first-time cross which flies out for a corner. Fernandes whips a corner into the box and Van Hecke wins the header, beating two Newcastle players to the ball. But Hornicek is there to parry the Dutchman’s close-range header away.

Robertson’s deep corner finds an unmarked Marmoush at the back stick. He takes a first-time shot, but his volley bounces wide of the near post. From that range, he needs to be getting that on target.

Marmoush has been on the periphery so far today. Spurs have looked threatening but they could be more attentive with possession at times, especially in midfield.

Van de Ven makes a crucial challenge to stop Wissa from fashioning a shooting opportunity inside the six-yard box after good build-up play from Nico and Elanga.

Newcastle are trying to get the ball forward quickly in this new “vertical” style of Matthias Jaissle but all it is doing at the moment is give it straight back to Tottenham Hotspur.

It has not been a fun first 20 minutes to watch from the visitors who have had little joy breaking through the lines and have invited pressure from Spurs.

The less said about their set piece delivery the better. Harvey Barnes has taken over corner duties from Bruno Guimaraes and has not managed to clear the first Tottenham defender yet.

Tottenham play a short corner and Botman’s headed clearance only finds Porro, who is lurking on the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. Porro’s catches the ball on the volley, but his strike flies over. The World Cup winner is playing with real confidence.

Jan Paul van Hecke has played a couple of exceptional forward passes in the early exchanges here. The £52m signing is already demonstrating his ability to start attacks from deep.

The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium screams for a free kick as Porro believes he was brought down by Willock on the edge of the penalty area. There’s minimal contact and referee Peter Bankes is not interested, waving play on.

Tottenham stream into Newcastle’s penalty area, and Tonali’s miscued makes it way through to Porro. He feints to send Miley flying, but Hall is there to make a goal-saving block and thwart Porro’s attempt. Spurs are beginning to grow into this contest and are currently in the ascendency.

Tel forces a flying save from Hornicek! Van Hecke picks out Marmoush with a piercing pass through Newcastle’s midfield, allowing the former Manchester Ciy man to tee up Tel. The winger takes the ball in his stride, cuts inside and whips a venomous effort at goal. Hornicek is up to the task and dives to make the stop.

Tonali has made an unsettled start to this game. He’s already given possession away on a couple of occasions and left space for Newcastle to exploit.

Nico then receives a yellow card on his Newcastle debut for apprehending Gray to stop Tottenham from counter-attacking.

Tonali and Tel give away the ball, allowing Newcastle to attack. Wissa cushions Dedic’s cross with an exquisite touch for Barnes, but the winger curls his effort comfortably off target and fails to trouble Kinsky.

Marmoush has been deployed as the central striker on his Tottenham debut, with Fernandes just behind him as the most advanced midfielder. Porro also looks to be starting on the right wing. It’s a very new-look frontline for Spurs following last weekend’s defeat to Brentford.

Sandro Tonali’s first meaningful action: badly underhitting a simple pass to Micky van de Ven. It resulted in the Spurs captain picking up a yellow card. The Newcastle fans are singing a song about Tonali in the away end, but I won’t repeat the lyrics here.

Tonali under-hits a pass back to Van de Ven, who flies in with a late challenge on Wissa, needlessly colliding with the Newcastle forward. The Spurs captain picks up an early booking. That it not the start he would have wanted.

Newcastle threaten straight away as Elanga nearly lifts an audacious lob over Kinsky from a tight angle. It doesn’t quite squeeze into the bottom corner and Spurs get back to concede a corner inside the first minute. Fernandes then bumps into Dedic off the ball, giving the visitors a free kick.

We are under way in North London. Can either side record their first Premier League win of the season after midweek Carabao Cup victories?

Captains Van de Ven and Thiaw lead their respective sides out onto the pitch. The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium is in full voice, with kick-off just minutes away.

With just under ten minutes until kick-off, here’s a recap of the two line-ups this evening.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Roberto De Zerbi has explained Sávio's absence from our matchday squad ℹ️📲 https://t.co/ACZscgieFg pic.twitter.com/ddGz2NveX3

“It was bad news yesterday before training in the afternoon because he suffered muscle fatigue and the medical staff obviously didn’t want to take a risk and I agree with them - it’s not the right moment, especially because he didn’t work in the last 10 days, for him 20 minutes against Charlton, maybe it was tough to rest for the days after but for the next game I think there are no problems.”

"Quality." 🤷‍♂️Matthias Jaissle on what Nico González adds to the Newcastle side 💬 pic.twitter.com/yjMBcr0pUm

"If I'm a Tottenham fan, this is the most excited I've been in MANY YEARS"Jamie Redknapp thinks that Spurs have built a strong squad that can compete in the Premier League 👀 pic.twitter.com/55Dwm7BaoE

It is not the sight of their former player Sandro Tonali in a Tottenham Hotspur shirt that will worry Newcastle United.

Omar Marmoush was only at Manchester City for 18 months but managed to score seven goals in just five appearances against Newcastle, including a hat-trick back in February 2025.

The Egyptian has moved to Spurs seeking regular first team football and will go up against the team he has enjoyed facing more than any other in English football.

Newcastle, of course, have a new manager Matthias Jaissle and are playing a different style of football under the German. Despite an unbeaten start in league and cup, the defence has not looked particularly assured.

That could make the ideal opponents for Spurs as they look to prove last season’s miserable home form is not going to continue into this one.

I’m fascinated to see how Newcastle play here. They were happy to sit back, soak up pressure and go direct in attack, mainly on the counter. That sort of approach could be even more effective away from home than at St James’ Park.

For me, it is far too early to say a summer of change has worked for Newcastle. We will have a better idea after this game.

Sandro Tonali’s departure from Newcastle United did not provoke the same extreme anger as Alexander Isak’s acrimonious move to Liverpool or the sadness of captain Bruno Guimarães’ switch to Arsenal. That is largely because nobody will miss him as much.

There is no doubt the Italy international’s determination to leave for Tottenham Hotspur did rankle supporters, especially given the club had stood by him during a 10-month betting ban, but Tonali was only a good player for Newcastle, not a great one.

Nico will make his NUFC debut today 🤩 pic.twitter.com/ilEM8w3Dwd

Roberto De Zerbi has said that Savio is missing because of “muscle fatigue.”

Tottenham had been hoping to see Savinho following his glittering cameo which yielded a goal and an assist against Charlton on Wednesday, but they will have to wait for his Premier League debut.

Both of these teams signed players from Manchester City this week. Omar Marmoush joined Spurs on a loan with a £60m obligation, while Nico Gonzalez moved to Newcastle for £52m. Both players have been thrown straight into the starting lineups of their respective teams.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

Recent recruit Nico Gonzalez begins in midfield and is set to make his Newcastle debut. Joe Willock scored in the Liverpool draw and is rewarded with a start, replacing the injured Will Osula.

Nico's in from the start! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/wx28WChueB

Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

Marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

Good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of new Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

As expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his new club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

Our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in new boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

Newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

#2068. Arsenal vs Hull City preview: Arteta sticks with winning formula as Gunners target another three points

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have resisted the temptation to rotate after their victory at Anfield, with Mikel Arteta naming the same starting XI for Saturday’s meeting with Hull City.

Arsenal welcome Championship side Hull City to the Emirates Stadium, looking to strengthen their grip on the top spot after collecting 24 points from their opening nine Premier League games. However, their tally of just 14 goals suggests Arteta’s side still have work to do in the final third.

Arteta has again chosen to partner Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães in defence. William Saliba was left out despite pre-match talk that he would be named in the starting XI. Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman are also missing from the squad.

Noni Madueke will carry the right. Tzolis starts on the opposite flank. Kai Havertz will lead the line. Viktor Gyökeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino add attacking options from the bench.

Arsenal predicted starting XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice, Ødegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis.

Substitutes: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Hincapié, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Gyökeres.

Hull are coming into this game ranked 11th in the league after five draws in their first nine games. They’ve not won in their last eight games but can cause problems for any opposition.

They look like playing a defensive game with Slater, Iroegbunam and Gourna-Douath in the midfield to protect the backline. McBurnie and Cho will give them some attacking options.

Hull starting XI: Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Stroud; Slater, Iroegbunam, Gourna-Douath; McBurnie, Cho.

Substitutes: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Gelhardt, Hjerto-Dahl, Norton-Cuffy, Herrington, Mouzakitis, Vaz.

McBurnie is just one booking away from suspension for the clash against Brighton on November 22 but may make an important impact in the physical battle with Gabriel.

Hull have not scored at the Emirates since 2014 but will look to turn that around. However, their main concern will be to ensure they keep Arsenal quiet for as long as possible.

Arsenal will need to find ways to break down the likely tight Hull backline.

Ødegaard and Rice will be key in keeping possession and creating chances, whilst Madueke and Tzolis will create width and movement.

Hull may be exposed to threat in case they are trapped in defence for too long, but Arteta can use Gyökeres if Havertz is having difficulties doing anything productive.

A win for Arsenal will give them a six-point lead. Manchester City will be looking to get all three points when they face Nottingham Forest later on Saturday.

The visitors will look to create an uncomfortable afternoon for the Gunners.

Arsenal have enough quality to take all three points, but Hull will not make it easy for them. I expect this to be a tight game, and the Gunners will win by a small margin.
